title: Be It My Only Wisdom Here
description: Be It My Only Wisdom Here in Tonic Solfa to MERIBAH, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 457 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “True Wisdom”, where the book credits them to Wesley's Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Particular Metre (8.8.6.8.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MERIBAH; any other Common Particular Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be it my on-ly wis-dom here, To serve the Lord with fil-ial fear, With lov-ing grat-i-tude; Su-pe-rior sense may I dis-play, By shun-ning ev-ery e-vil way, And walk-ing in the good.

lines: Be it my only wisdom here,
To serve the Lord with filial fear,
O may I still from sin depart!
And let me through thy Spirit know
And find my way to heaven.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MERIBAH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
